summary: A Session-2 independent review of Session-1 finding S1-F033, covering the Epistemic Intermediate Representation (EIR), the corpus's only cost/economics-based justification for a Kernel, three converging admission-condition lenses (standing, prerequisite presence, context sufficiency), a retroactive-knowledge-state consequence, and a conditional proposal to narrow an earlier semi-Markov tension.

summary: A Session-2 register of six cross-track observations (X-001..X-006) about relationships between the extraction, review, research, architecture and adjudication tracks: porous scope exclusions, a research finding reshaping adjudication topology, the reviewer's own standing hypothesis possibly descending from the corpus it tests, three incompatible senses of 'Zero lens', and a full adjudication-to-research-to-review laundering round trip, plus an addendum adopting an extent/contents/surrounding-law/constitutional (A-E) instrument while refusing to treat its corpus appearance as corroboration.

Explicitly never routed into corpus findings or adjudication.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F034 on 'sufficient state' (Astrom's stochastic-control concept applied to KnowledgeOS), showing it sharpens a previously-measured gap about authority validity at a historical point in time, confirming and compounding the Zero-lens definition-lag finding, endorsing a five-way Assessment non-collapse and a lens-honesty disclaimer, but challenging Session 1's claim that decision-relative adequacy was independently arrived at twice.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F001 (an authority-temporal-semantics gap measured across 20 grants, 0/20 carrying temporal properties), reclassifying the finding as UNREPRESENTED rather than a measured rate, sharpening it from 'not addressed' to 'attached to the wrong object' (the claim is time-indexed via TemporalValidity, the authority reference is not), verifying against v1.1 law that no existing control duplicates the concern, and reaching the register's strongest verdict to date: IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION, because a revoked authority's past admissions become permanently unauditable and irreversibly so. A later 2026-08-28 update ties this to S1-F034's 'sufficient state' as the missing sufficiency criterion, without changing the verdict.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F035, confirming that counterfactual robustness supplies a constructive procedure for separating validation evidence from construction evidence, praising an honest no-material-finding register, but challenging a claimed three-carrier composite (route, acquisition procedure, role) by arguing route and acquisition method may be the same carrier already present in law, and reclassifying an 'inter-level knowledge' claim from a seventh genus of knowledge to an altitude claim.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F036, called the corpus's strongest artifact and one Session 1 nearly lost on a first shallow pass (finding only ~15% of it before a full re-read recovered ten findings). Substantively, it adds a decidable membership test with a genuinely executed 24-row capability table (the only place in the corpus a membership criterion is actually run), a positive epistemic-honesty formulation ('reconstructible epistemology') consistent with existing law's rejection of a truth oracle, and a six-way temporal-role split that supplies the missing shape for the previously-verified authority-temporal-validity gap (three independent routes now converge on the same hole).

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F037's three modelling prohibitions (don't decompose primitives into aggregates, don't derive ontology from representation format, don't solve a primitive by renaming it), a Knowledge-Space boundary defined as observer-relative (abstraction/purpose/scope/observability, distinct from the Kernel-extent boundary sense), a seven-way classification question, and a claim that participants transform rather than merely view Knowledge Space; challenges a claimed three-way identity-position rivalry by dissolving it into three different questions rather than one contested proposition.

summary: A Python testing script (GN-46 mathematical verification) that independently re-implements EXP-01's four evidence-aggregation operators (MAX, WEIGHTED_MEAN, SATURATING, BAYES_LIKE) and re-derives, under two explicit semantics (RAW: no preprocessing; PIPE: dependency/equivalence collapse plus relevance filtering before the operator), whether each satisfies eight designed properties (A duplicate invariance, B independent corroboration, C order invariance, D associativity, E contradiction preservation, F dependency awareness, G irrelevance, H temporal validity) plus a bounded-[0,1] check, an adversarial 100-duplicate stress test, and a calibration demonstration.
contribution_assessment: A primary mathematical/testing artifact reproducing prior reasoning independently without modifying any existing verdict or CSV; explicitly designed to resolve a historical discrepancy between a prose verdict and a CSV about which aggregation operators pass which properties (GN-27) by showing that a RAW/PIPE semantic split explains the discrepancy, and that the corpus's negative conclusion (no simple scalar operator suffices as an epistemic foundation) depends on criterion E plus pre-operator dependency handling plus a calibration caution, not on the seven-column pass/fail matrix alone.

summary: The captured console output of running exp01_recheck.py: per-property RAW/PIPE pass/fail results for all four aggregation operators, a comparison table against a historical verdict table and a historical CSV, and a closing reading concluding the CSV mixes RAW/PIPE semantics inconsistently across cells while the historical verdict's prose is internally consistent, and that the corpus's negative conclusion about scalar operators is confirmed and in fact provable from the combination of results, not from the seven-column matrix alone.
contribution_assessment: Concrete numeric evidence: under RAW semantics every operator fails duplicate/dependency/irrelevance handling (properties A, F, G) except where noted, while under PIPE semantics all four pass A, F, G, and H; SATURATING and BAYES_LIKE both pass all seven of the historically-tracked columns, yet SATURATING still assigns 0.9718 to ten independent weak (s=0.3) items with no underlying probability model, and BAYES_LIKE assigns 0.9846 to a 3-item dependent evidence chain treated as independent versus the correct single-source value of 0.8000 -- concrete numerical demonstrations of double-counting/overconfidence that ground the paper's calibration caution.

summary: A GN-46 mathematical-verification Python script that gives a reference implementation of Zero(K, EC) from the ratified 025d Formal Zero Algebra, reruns 025d's own falsification tests (25D.38 T1-T8) as executed code rather than declared PASSes, reproduces the source's own worked example (25D.8), and demonstrates the Gamma-sufficiency ('Insufficient') status and a scalar-collapse counterexample as executable semantics.
contribution_assessment: A primary computability witness: shows Zero(K,EC) is a total, terminating aggregation over a finite requirement set relative to per-requirement evaluators treated as oracles (complexity O(|R| * cost(evaluate))), explicitly does not establish that the evaluators themselves (Gamma semantics, HumanAuthorization oracles) or the construction of EC (eta) are computable -- naming these open questions OQ-1/AF-F-1 -- and demonstrates a status ('Insufficient') plus two full status classes (Stale, Prohibited) that a ratified four-arm summary vocabulary cannot express (named the PF-1 loss), here shown as executable semantics rather than prose.

summary: The captured console output of running zero_reference.py: the §25D.8 worked example reproduced exactly, all eight 25D.38 falsification tests (T1-T8) passing when actually executed, the Gamma-sufficiency Insufficient demonstration passing, the scalar-collapse counterexample passing, and the closing computability verdict.
contribution_assessment: Confirms numerically, as executed output, every claim made in the paired script (S1317): the worked example matches exactly, all eight historically declared-only falsification tests actually pass when run as code, and the PF-1 vocabulary loss and scalar-collapse counterexample are demonstrated with concrete values rather than asserted in prose.

summary: A speculative, verse-by-verse mathematical derivation mapping all of Bhagavad-gita Chapter 4 (provenance, divine memory, intervention, reward, caste/duty, non-attachment, action/inaction duality, the wise person's state, multiple worship/evidence paths, epistemic benefit, teacher-student learning, and faith/doubt/closure) onto proposed KnowledgeOS mathematical structures and matching Python class sketches, culminating in an integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class and a single closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment).
contribution_assessment: An exploratory, single-sourced, unverified formalization exercise: for each of twelve verse groups it invents named functions/equations (e.g. exponential knowledge decay, an intervention trigger threshold, an epistemic reward step function, a non-attachment/bondage integral, a wise-person state vector, a faith/doubt ratio, a 'sword of wisdom' derivative) with no derivation from first principles, no calibration, and several mathematically dubious constructions (division by uncertainty that can be zero, a final equation dividing by a sum that can be zero, units left undefined throughout); it also sketches a matching Python implementation for every formalization and a final orchestrating GitaKnowledgeOS.evolve() pipeline tying in the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F038, confirming 'store the substrate, compute the measure' as an already-lawful principle (Confidence is structured, never a scalar) and elevating a checkable point-in-time reconstruction test ('what did we know at 13:47?') to the register's single highest-value unrun action, since it could resolve five of six open IMPLEMENTATION QUESTIONs at once; also confirms an absence-must-not-become-a-state finding and a possible-worlds storage refusal, but challenges a projection-consistency invariant as single-sourced and doubly contradicted from within the corpus itself.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F039's claim that the Kernel preserves discrimination-enabling structures without itself reasoning, presented as four independent arrivals; confirms a genuinely novel technical minimality argument (Brachman & Levesque: an unbounded Knowledge Space vs a necessarily finite projection) and Williamson's refusal of reductive knowledge-definition, but challenges the 'four independent arrivals' framing as really about two (two KR&R textbook citations share one disciplinary prior), and flags that Searle's institutional counting-as is a fourth, differently-grounded position on context that both joins an existing temporal-validity cluster and creates unresolved tension with a separately-challenged projection-consistency invariant.
contribution_assessment: Identifies the only non-assertive, non-philosophical technical argument for Kernel minimality found across 40 reviewed artifacts (finite projections of an unbounded Knowledge Space); reduces an over-counted four-way convergence to two independent traditions by the same disciplinary-prior-sharing correction applied elsewhere in this register; and surfaces that institutionally-conferred status (Searle's counting-as) is an authority claim wearing a context label, with a validity period by construction, joining the register's ongoing authority-temporal cluster.

summary: The Session-2 review register's master index and adopted framework (established on HPA direction, 2026-08-25): a ten-lens review discipline (DDD, Zero, Provenance, Temporal, Authority, Evidence/justification, Boundary/altitude, Identity, Claim/hypothesis, Knowledge/Knowledge Space) with two standing override rules on contradictions and reconciliations; a full index of 40 per-artifact reviews plus cross-track observations and method observations (M-1 through M-8); and closing summary statistics after all 40 Session-1 findings were reviewed, including a complete implementation-verdict tally, a list of thirteen dissolved apparent contradictions against two surviving constitutional tensions, and four specified-but-never-run adversarial instruments.

summary: A Session-2 review of S1-F040, the corpus's only complete falsification cycle: a v0.1 'projection = measure' proposal refuted six independent ways in about 78 minutes and resolved (by its own proposer) into 'relational/logical structure as the mathematical core, with metric/topology/probability/measure/statistics/causal models as regimes'. Confirms the refutation sequence as perspective-diverse in a way never applied to the corpus's own Kernel formulations, confirms Roberts' measurement-as-homomorphism as a genuinely independent arrival at 'store the substrate, compute the measure', and identifies why this proposer-driven falsification actually resolved where a peer-commissioned one (S1-F016) did not; but reclassifies the resolution's apparent three-day convergence with a day-one position (S1-F005) as not a new independent arrival at all -- only its reasons are new.
contribution_assessment: The review's sharpest methodological product is M-8: the corpus attacked its own mathematics with six independent refutations in 78 minutes but has run zero adversarial passes over its eight Kernel formulations across four days, and the one falsification that was commissioned against a Kernel formulation (S1-F016) was later re-asserted against ten hours later without being engaged -- while this cascade resolved precisely because its proposer, not an outside party, performed the refutation and resolution.

summary: GN-46 (an extension of GN-43), an independent mathematical/statistical/computational verification report auditing the ratified KnowledgeOS architecture's entire mathematical content (v0.2, FA-1..9, Edition-2 Part III, and ~14 numbered sources) against a strict verify-not-repair mandate, producing a 16-object mathematical inventory, a full definition/derivation/computability/statistical/metric/measure/entropy/topology/operator audit, an independent EXP-01 recheck, a source-vs-synthesis compression audit (PF-1..9), 22 new or confirmed findings (MV-F-1..22), and final verdicts of MATHEMATICALLY SOUND WITH QUALIFICATIONS for the ratified boundary/invariant layer, MATHEMATICALLY UNDER-SPECIFIED for the formal-object layer, and NOT COMPUTATIONALLY REALIZED for the architecture as a system.
contribution_assessment: The authoritative synthesis tying together every mathematical-tests script in this batch (exp01_recheck, zero_reference, ladder_dc_reference): confirms the corpus's load-bearing mathematics is honest but thin and sound as stated, confirms the EXP-01 negative verdict is not only reproduced but provable, and produces genuinely new findings not previously registered anywhere -- most importantly that the ratified Decision Contract six-tuple has no ratified admissibility law of its own (MV-F-5), that the stratification loop's induction has no genesis base case (MV-F-8, confirming AF-F-14 formally), that four scattered identity/equality questions (evidence equivalence, state equality, frame equivalence, requirement identity) are really one missing foundation (MV-F-22, an 'identity calculus'), and that PF-1's compression from nine statuses to four silently dropped three formally load-bearing statuses (Insufficient, Stale, Prohibited).
